questions.question: What type of relationship does inheritance represent between a child class and a parent class?
options: A "has-a" relationship (e.g., a Car has-a Engine)
An "is-a" relationship (e.g., a Dog is-a Animal)
A "uses-a" relationship (e.g., a Programmer uses-a Computer)
A "contains-a" relationship (e.g., a Library contains-a Book)
questions.explanation: Inheritance creates an "is-a" relationship. The child class is a more specific version of the parent class. A Dog is a specific type of Animal, so Dog inherits from Animal.

questions.question: What is the correct syntax to create a class called `Poodle` that inherits from a class called `Dog`?
questions.explanation: In Python, inheritance is specified by placing the parent class name in parentheses after the child class name: `class Child(Parent):`.
